Honoring Martin Luther King Jr. Day

Today is a reminder that leadership is not defined by title or position — it’s defined by courage, conviction, and compassion.

Dr. King challenged us to lead with empathy, to confront injustice without hatred, and to believe that meaningful change begins with everyday choices. His words still ring true:

“Darkness cannot drive out darkness; only light can do that.”

In our work, our communities, and our families, may we choose to be that light — even when it’s uncomfortable, even when it requires us to listen more than we speak, and even when progress feels slow.

Today, and every day, let’s commit to building systems, cultures, and futures rooted in dignity, equity, and humanity.

💚

#MLKDay #LeadershipWithPurpose #ServiceAboveSelf #EquityAndJustice #LeadWithLight #LeMayFusionGroup

You can add marketing.
You can add people.
You can add tools.

But if leadership priorities, operations, and financial discipline aren’t clear, growth doesn't solve problems - it magnifies them.

That’s why my work through LeMay Fusion Group stays closely aligned with TAG Marketing Group.

LFG focuses on helping businesses get aligned — leadership, people, process, and performance.

TAG focuses on translating that clarity into growth strategy and momentum.
Different strengths. Shared standards. One aligned approach.

When the foundation is right, growth becomes far more predictable — and far less painful.

For over 20 years, I led sales teams across seven states—working side by side with thousands of people, day in and day out.

At the height of my career, I was communicating with my team for up to 12 hours a day—calls, emails, meetings, strategy sessions, crisis management, check-ins, coaching.
That’s nearly 75% of my waking hours, seven days a week.   In sales there’s no days off.  Yeah you weren’t visiting stores but business was still open, sales still needed to be pushed and people would still have problems.  

Meanwhile, my family—my wife and three young kids—got the scraps.
A rushed breakfast.
A few distracted minutes at dinner.
Maybe a story at bedtime—if I wasn’t finishing a deck or answering one more email.

10–15% of my daily attention. That’s all they got.

But I told myself what so many of us do:
“I’m doing it for them.”
“This is what leadership requires.”
“I’ll find balance later.”

Then life hit me hard. My health failed. I was forced to step away.

And here’s the truth no one tells you:

The second you leave… 90% of the people you gave your time to disappear.
Not because they’re bad people—but because the connection was built on the job, not on something deeper.
Without the meetings, the mission, the shared grind… the relationship fades.

That’s when it hits you:

You gave the best of yourself to people who were only ever meant to be temporary.

This post isn’t about bitterness. It’s about perspective.

Yes, work hard. Build something that matters.
But don’t sacrifice the people and parts of yourself that last beyond the title.

Because when the job ends—and it will—you’ll realize:
	•	The emails stop.
	•	The phone quiets.
	•	The “work family” moves on.
But your kids? They still need their dad.
Your partner? Still wants your presence.
And your identity? Still matters without the badge.

Don’t wait for life to knock you down to realize what truly matters.

Balance isn’t weakness. It’s wisdom.

After 20+ years in leadership, I never imagined my toughest battle would be with the very system I thought I could trust.

A little over a year ago, my life began to unravel. At the time, I thought the worst thing I was facing was the acquisition of a company I loved — a company we had built with heart, grit, and an incredible team. I watched as leadership was dismantled, not by performance, but by politics. That loss hit hard. My career had always been everything to me.

But that was only the beginning.

What started as tailbone pain quickly spiraled into full-body dysfunction — nerve pain, cognitive decline, bowel and bladder dysfunction, and unbearable suffering. I visited 12 hospitals, underwent two spinal fusions, and was repeatedly told it was “stress” or “anxiety.”

It wasn’t.

I had Tethered Cord Syndrome — a rare neurological condition most doctors overlook in adults.

This past Tuesday, I underwent spinal cord detethering surgery. The emotional, physical, and financial toll of being ignored for so long has been profound. It’s impacted my body, my marriage,— and most painfully — my children. Much of the damage done to my autonomic and central nervous system is irreversible.

That’s why I wrote Tethered to a Broken System — not just to share my story, but to shine a light on a massive blind spot in our healthcare system and give a voice to the unheard.   It’s not just about this disease.   It’s about how truly BROKEN the medical and insurance system are.    I’ve heard people neeeding tests that could save their lives that a doctor can’t write orders for because their condition has met insurance requirements for the test.   

After joining online communities and connecting with others, I realized I’m far from alone. Tens of thousands go undiagnosed or misdiagnosed each year, often receiving incorrect treatments or undergoing unnecessary surgeries — like I did.

This book is for anyone who’s been dismissed, misdiagnosed, or gaslit by the system meant to help them. It’s raw, real, and written with purpose.

If you’ve ever felt alone in your medical journey — this is for you. And if you’re a leader in healthcare, this is a wake-up call. Stop assuming it’s always anxiety or drug-seeking behavior when scans and labs don’t give you easy answers. Hundreds of conditions fall through the cracks of a system too broken to see them.

I always believed my life’s mission was to develop people into great leaders. But it turns out, God had something else in mind.

This week, I head into my third spinal surgery in just 12 months.

Three surgeries. One year.
A journey I never saw coming—and one I pray is finally coming to an end.

I now have:
	•	A metal plate in my neck
	•	Nine screws
	•	Two artificial discs
	•	A metal plate in my lower back
	•	Nine more screws
	•	One more artificial disc

And this week, I go under the knife again—this time to have my spinal cord detethered.

It’s a condition I was likely born with, but never knew existed. A condition that’s been silently pulling on my spinal cord, damaging nerves and disrupting my body in ways I can’t begin to describe. A condition that’s rarely taught, rarely looked for, and almost never caught. And because of that, I’ve suffered—not from neglect, but from a system that didn’t know what to look for.

Over the past year and a half, my world has shifted.
I’ve gone from a life of momentum, leadership, and vision… to a life focused entirely on survival.

The roles I was proud of—husband, father, leader, builder—collided with a body that was breaking down faster than doctors could explain.

When your health is stripped away, you learn very quickly what really matters.

And what matters most is time.
Not money.
Not status.
Not titles.
Not things.

Time.

Time with your children—before they grow up.
Time with your spouse—before another year passes.
Time to walk, to breathe, to chase a dream—before it slips away.
Time you think you’ll have… but often don’t.

This year has broken me wide open.
It’s shown me that nothing is promised—not even the ability to get out of bed, to stand without pain, or to hug your kids without wincing. It’s also shown me how resilient the human spirit is when you’re forced to rebuild from the ground up.

We all say we’ll chase our dreams “when the time is right.”

After the next promotion.
After the kids are older.
After life slows down.

But here’s the truth: Life doesn’t wait.
And neither should you.

If there’s something you feel called to do—
Start the business.
Write the book.
Take the trip.
Make the move.
Heal the relationship.

Don’t wait for “someday.”
Do it now.

Because none of us are guaranteed a tomorrow where our spine still works… where our energy still shows up… where our dreams are still in reach.

This post isn’t about struggle.
It’s about awakening.

If I can walk away from this third surgery with anything, I hope it’s this:
	•	To live fully present
	•	To be radically grateful
	•	And to use my time with purpose

I promised myself over the last 16 months:
If they ever found the cause… if they could fix me… I would live my life differently.

It looks like I’m going to have to gladly uphold my end of the bargain.

I wouldn’t wish what I’ve gone through on anyone.

But I do hope you get that moment—the one where everything becomes clear—and you finally realize what’s truly important in this life.

Just promise me you won’t wait until it’s too late.

Darkness doesn’t like the light. 

Negativity doesn’t like positivity. 

I have a friend who has a newsletter he sends out periodically. 

His messages are positive and life giving. 

He’s a force for good. 

His most recent newsletter had a person who wrote him telling him he was going to unsubscribe after 3 years of following him because his messages were too positive….

No one, he claims, can be that positive all the time. 

So…he doesn’t want that kind of positive message in his inbox. 

Bye Felicia! 

I told my friend- 
Keep shining! 
The world needs more light - not less! 

There is too much negativity and darkness around us. 

The internet and faceless comments have given people the ability to drop negativity bombs 💣 in our comments that aim to dim the light. 

People need more positivity in their life. 

Pollyanna’s “Glad Game” may be a little extreme…

But let me tell you something…

If you try playing the “Glad Game” and look for the silver lining or the part of your circumstance to be grateful for…

I can almost guarantee you that your life will be better. 

Your mental health will be better. 

If you are looking for a job…
Or new opportunities l…
Or a relationship…

It’ll make you more desirable and hireable. 

Putting out a positive message for others and in your mind does nothing but dispel the darkness around you. 

So…

Shine bright! 

Keep shining! 

Don’t let the negativity/energy vampires win!!  

Let’s go!!

I see it all the time.
 
Capable people second-guessing themselves.
Strong leaders downplaying what they bring.
Teams missing how much value is sitting right in front of them.

When people start to see their strengths clearly, everything changes.

Confidence grows.
Communication improves.
Momentum follows.

We each carry more potential than we tend to give ourselves credit for.

One of the biggest mistakes I see growing businesses make is trying to scale activity before they’ve aligned the business underneath it.

You can add marketing.
You can add people.
You can add tools.

But if leadership priorities, operations, and financial discipline aren’t clear, growth doesn't solve problems - it magnifies them.

That’s why my work through LeMay Fusion Group stays closely aligned with TAG Marketing Group.

LFG focuses on helping businesses get aligned — leadership, people, process, and performance.

TAG focuses on translating that clarity into growth strategy and momentum.
Different strengths. Shared standards. One aligned approach.

When the foundation is right, growth becomes far more predictable — and far less painful.

Over the years, one thing has become very clear to me:
Most growth problems aren’t marketing problems.
They’re alignment problems.

I’ve watched businesses invest in marketing before leadership, operations, and priorities were truly aligned—and then wonder why the results didn’t stick.

That’s why LeMay Fusion Group and TAG Marketing Group operate so closely together.
LeMay Fusion Group focuses on leadership alignment, people, process, and financial discipline.

TAG Marketing Group focuses on turning that clarity into real growth—through positioning, strategy, and Fractional CMO leadership.

Different focus areas. One shared philosophy:
Growth works when strategy and execution are grounded in how a business actually runs.

We’ve been working this way for a long time.
We’re simply being more intentional about saying it out loud.
